name: lora-merge
desc: Free, open-source LoRA merger for Windows — blend adapters into a base model at custom weights, export safetensors. 100 MB portable, MIT.
features: ✅ **Weight sliders per adapter** — stack up to five LoRAs and set each blend ratio from zero to full
✅ **Base model safe mode** — merges onto a copy and verifies the output loads before you delete anything
✅ **Safetensors in, safetensors out** — keeps metadata and formatting, not a pickle-era mess
✅ **Preset library** — save favorite blends under names and rerun them after a base model update
✅ **Validation pass** — tensor count and shape check against the base before writing gigabytes
✅ **GPU or CPU merge** — uses VRAM when available and falls back to RAM on cards with no headroom
✅ **100 MB self-contained exe** — runtime and merge backend bundled, portable, offline, MIT
compare: | Feature | **lora-merge** | kohya sd-scripts | PEFT scripts | Web merge tools |
| Price | **Free, MIT** | Free, OSS | Free, OSS | Free accounts |
| GUI with per-adapter sliders | **Yes** | Complex config | No | Partial
| Portable, no install | **Yes, 100 MB** | Python env | Python env | Upload required
faqQ: how to merge multiple LoRAs into one model offline?
faqA: There is no way around doing it in Python or uploading multi-GB checkpoints to a website. lora-merge stacks up to five adapters with per-adapter weights, validates tensor shapes against the base and writes a clean safetensors file. It is a 100 MB portable exe, MIT, fully offline, and your models never leave the disk.
